title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-18
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v10.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 12/18/73 Tampa show with a smoking second set (WRS > Dark Star > Eyes > Wharf Rat) and superb Charlie Miller transfer.
ai_review.review: The recording is a crystal‑clear, stereo soundboard mastered by Charlie Miller that preserves the band’s full dynamics while only showing minor audience patches. Musically the night shines especially in the second set – Weather Report Suite into Dark Star, the epic Eyes of the World sequence and a fiery Wharf Rat – making it one of the standout performances of 1973.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen enthusiastic reviews (mostly 5‑star) praise both the musical performance and the Miller soundboard transfer; show quality is rated as exceptional, recording quality as excellent, yielding a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp stereo mix, very clear instrument separation, praised Charlie Miller transfer as a "masterpiece"; minor audience patch around 14:20 noted but not detrimental.

poor_songs: Beat It On Down the Line (sluggish)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set opens strong with a rare Tennessee Jed but settles into a slower, laid‑back groove; second set erupts with jazzy segues and high‑energy peaks, delivering an overall arc that builds to a spectacular climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for confident, soaring solo work (especially on Let It Grow/Wharf Rat) and strong vocal phrasing; noted as one of his best performances of the year.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as "monster" bass with aggressive lower‑register leads; highlighted for tight interplay during Eyes of the World and driving the second‑set energy.
band_member_comments.Bob: Commended for slashing, jazzy leads and a powerful solo on China Cat > Rider; noted for dynamic interplay with Jerry throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is praised for ready piano work (Me & My Uncle, fills) and overall solid keyboard presence despite Donna Jean’s absence.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann noted as "in the pocket" with a tight drum solo that propels into Eyes of the World; rhythm section described as solid throughout.
